blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Small language models (SLMs) can run on commodity hardware and support privacy-preserving, on-premises clinical deployment, but their medical explanations are often short and poorly structured compared with large language models. Recent supervised approaches such as Meerkat transfer chain-of-thought reasoning into 7B-8B backbones, yet their training objective does not directly target the style or organization of the generated rationales. Building on the instruction-tuned Mistral-7B backbone, we investigate whether a lightweight reinforcement learning (RL) step can improve explanation structure without human preference labels.We apply Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with LoRA adaptation to 2,000 Meerkat-derived medical prompts, guided by a simple self-supervised reward that favors longer, lexically diverse, and well-punctuated responses while penalizing very short ones. Training for about 170 PPO steps on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU yields a stable increase in the average reward. Quantitative and qualitative comparisons show that the RL-tuned model produces longer, more organized, multi-point explanations while preserving the underlying medical content.We discuss the promise and the limitations of self-rewarded RL for shaping the style of medical explanations.

medicine. Wu et al. (2023) ; Xie et al. (2024) While these models improve the

align LLMs with human preferences and downstream objectives. Proximal Policy

consists of a scalar quality signal (such as a human preference score) as well

reference model. Ziegler et al. (2019) ; Ouyang et al. (2022)

and logic of reasoning traces, the surface features such as the number of words
and punctuation are not explicitly optimized

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
We have outlined a reinforcement learning process that uses PPO with a minimal
LoRA adaptation to fine-tune a 7B parameter instruction-tuned language model in
a medical context, with a self-supervised reward function that promotes longer,
more diverse, and sentence-structured explanations. Our process was successful
in optimizing a proxy reward function over a subset of Meerkat’s medical
instruction data, producing qualitatively better structured explanations over
real-world clinical data. Although effective for influencing explanation style
in small medical language models, this process is, by itself, not sufficient as
